config.title: Build feature flag utility with variants

intro.title: Build feature flag utility with variants
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple feature flag utility that allows you to toggle different versions (variants) of a feature in your JavaScript application. You'll learn how to use objects to store configuration data and conditional logic to control which variant is active. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, conditional statements (if/else), and functions. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that can help manage feature rollouts or A/B testing in your projects.
intro.usecase: Feature flags with variants are used by companies like Netflix and Amazon to test different UI designs before full rollout. Developers implement them in dashboards to toggle between chart layouts or data visualizations, and in e-commerce product pages to A/B test button colors or placement. This pattern allows gradual feature releases, enabling teams to measure performance impact and roll back changes instantly if issues arise.

objectives: Implement a feature flag function that checks if a feature is enabled
Construct a feature flag configuration object with variant values
Initialize a feature flag utility with default and custom configurations
Apply conditional logic to render different UI components based on feature flags
Manipulate feature flag states to toggle features on and off
Integrate feature flags into a simple application to control feature visibility
Configure feature variants to enable A/B testing scenarios

steps.title: Create feature flag configuration object
steps.instruction: Create a JavaScript object named 'featureFlags' that will store all feature flag configurations with their variants and status.
steps.hint: Start by declaring a constant variable named 'featureFlags' and assign it an empty object {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a featureFlags object ready to hold your feature flag configurations.
successCriteria: A constant named 'featureFlags' is declared and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've declared a constant named 'featureFlags' and assigned it an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a JavaScript object named 'featureFlags' to store feature flag configurations.

steps.title: Add first feature flag with variants
steps.instruction: Add a property 'darkMode' to your featureFlags object with variants 'on', 'off', and 'auto', and a default status of false.
steps.hint: Add a new property to the featureFlags object with the key 'darkMode' and an object as its value containing 'variants' and 'default' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The featureFlags object will have a darkMode property with variants array and default value.
successCriteria: The featureFlags object contains a darkMode property with variants ['on', 'off', 'auto'] and default set to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the darkMode property, but check that it has both 'variants' and 'default' properties with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The darkMode property is missing or doesn't have the required structure. Make sure to add it with variants and default properties.

steps.title: Add second feature flag with variants
steps.instruction: Add a property named 'newDashboard' to the featureFlags object with variants 'v1', 'v2', and 'v3', and a default status of true.
steps.hint: Add a new property after the darkMode property. The property should be an object with variants and default keys.
steps.expectedOutcome: The featureFlags object will have two properties: darkMode and newDashboard, each with their own variants and default values.
successCriteria: The featureFlags object contains a newDashboard property with variants ['v1', 'v2', 'v3'] and default: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the newDashboard property, but check that it has the correct variants array and default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The newDashboard property is missing or has incorrect structure. It should be an object with variants and default keys.

steps.title: Create feature flag utility function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'isFeatureEnabled' that takes a feature name as a parameter and returns the enabled status of that feature from the featureFlags object.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a parameter (like 'featureName') and accesses the featureFlags object to return the feature's status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named isFeatureEnabled is defined that can check the status of a feature flag by name.
successCriteria: The function isFeatureEnabled is created, takes a parameter, and returns the feature's status from featureFlags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'isFeatureEnabled' and takes a parameter to accept the feature name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a function named 'isFeatureEnabled' that accepts a feature name parameter and returns the feature's status from the featureFlags object.

steps.title: Create variant selection function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'getFeatureVariant' that takes a feature name as a parameter and returns the current variant from the featureFlags object. For now, just return the default variant.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts one parameter (featureName) and returns featureFlags[featureName].default.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named getFeatureVariant is defined that returns the default variant from the featureFlags object.
successCriteria: The getFeatureVariant function exists, accepts a featureName parameter, and returns featureFlags[featureName].default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'getFeatureVariant' and returns the default variant from the featureFlags object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'getFeatureVariant', given it a parameter, and returned the default variant from the featureFlags object.

steps.title: Create toggle feature function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'toggleFeature' that takes a feature name as a parameter and toggles its enabled status in the featureFlags object.
steps.hint: The function should accept a feature name string, find that feature in the featureFlags object, and flip its enabled property between true and false.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleFeature function that can change the enabled status of any feature in the featureFlags object.
successCriteria: The toggleFeature function is defined, accepts a feature name parameter, and toggles the enabled property of that feature in featureFlags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleFeature function properly accesses the feature in featureFlags and flips its enabled property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleFeature function isn't quite right. It should accept a feature name and toggle that feature's enabled status in the featureFlags object.

steps.title: Create set variant function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'setFeatureVariant' that takes a feature name and a variant value, and updates the variant in the featureFlags object.
steps.hint: Define a function with two parameters: featureName and variant. Inside, check if the feature exists in featureFlags and if the variant is valid, then update the default property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named setFeatureVariant that updates the default variant of a feature flag.
successCriteria: The setFeatureVariant function is defined with two parameters, validates the feature and variant, and updates the default property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function validates both the feature existence and variant validity before updating.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that it takes two parameters and properly updates the featureFlags object.

steps.title: Create demo function to test feature flags
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'demoFeatureFlags' that demonstrates using all the utility functions with the configured feature flags.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls each utility function with appropriate arguments and logs or returns the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'demoFeatureFlags' is created that demonstrates using the feature flag utility functions.
successCriteria: The 'demoFeatureFlags' function is defined and calls at least one of the utility functions with the 'featureFlags' configuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the demo function, but make sure it calls at least one of the utility functions with the feature flags configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The demo function isn't properly defined. Create a function named 'demoFeatureFlags' that demonstrates using the utility functions.

steps.title: Call demo function and log results
steps.instruction: Call the demoFeatureFlags function and log its return value to the console.
steps.hint: Use console.log() with the function call as its argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The demoFeatureFlags function will be called and its return value will be displayed in the console.
successCriteria: demoFeatureFlags is called and its return value is logged using console.log.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling demoFeatureFlags() and logging the result with console.log().
steps.feedbackWrong: call the demoFeatureFlags function and log its return value to the console.

steps.title: Export the utility functions
steps.instruction: Export the featureFlags object and all four utility functions (isFeatureEnabled, getFeatureVariant, toggleFeature, setFeatureVariant) so they can be imported in other files.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before each declaration, or use a single export statement at the end.
steps.expectedOutcome: The feature flag configuration and utility functions are exported and ready to be used in other modules.
successCriteria: featureFlags, isFeatureEnabled, getFeatureVariant, toggleFeature, and setFeatureVariant are all exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some items, but make sure to export all five: featureFlags, isFeatureEnabled, getFeatureVariant, toggleFeature, and setFeatureVariant.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incomplete. Ensure you export the featureFlags object and all four utility functions.
